$comment: The naming trap. This spec is IDENTICAL to demo.spec.json except for its name — every other field is the one that scaffolds the frozen golden, so it is valid on every axis check-spec grades. The only defect is that `forge` says nothing about counting a repository, and a name that says nothing is the defect no lint downstream can see: it survives CI, ships, and has to be renamed later, which is what happened to forge, assay and smith in this very repo. If check-spec ever accepts this file, the name rule has been weakened rather than the input fixed.
name: forge
summary: Count what a repository owes you — open PRs, stale branches, unreleased commits — as one table.
description: Report what a repository currently owes: open pull requests and how long each has waited, branches merged but never deleted, and commits sitting on main with no release tag. Use when the user asks "what's outstanding", "any stale branches", "what hasn't shipped", or wants a repo hygiene check before a release.
oneRule: Never report a count you did not read from the repository itself — an estimate is a guess wearing a number.

commands.name: detect
commands.does: the repo's remote, default branch and release convention, as one table

commands.name: count
commands.does: open PRs, stale branches and unreleased commits, each with its age

nondeterministic.step: decide which of the counts actually matters today
nondeterministic.why: urgency is context no file records
the same numbers mean different things before and after a release

references.is: the fixed shape of a forge report

evalPlan.pinnedAgainst: a real forge run against a repository with known counts
evalPlan.catches: a count silently going to zero, which reads as good news
reporting zeroes instead of refusing, which is the failure that looks like success
